# Native compact application layouts

`make linux-compact-workspace-test` now uses the native assembled application harness. Each case starts a fresh private X11 session so window allocation, scale, focus, clipboard and persisted selection cannot leak between cases. The existing application/Live targets keep their shared eleven-workflow/122-state run; compact adds eleven separate workflows/22 layout-and-reopen states.

The immutable reference is untouched v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. The external observer imports the downloaded release, verifies all 77 modules against that commit before activation, and checks imported paths and hashes after shutdown. Actual application actions, GTK controls and stores run against native PCM/Codex processes and loopback HTTP. No application handler, scheduler or renderer is replaced. Temporary reference observers stay under ignored `tmp/` and are not required by the native target or package.

[Released compact observations](released-application-compact.json), SHA-256 `70457137ea83087576671e20944f848386ba913391f7f6ab2bdd3429f548f723`, retain exact layouts, labels, sensitivity, source/draft/document/store/clipboard contents, reopened results, seven speech requests and seven Codex turns. WAV bodies retain byte counts and SHA-256 digests; complete rewrite input/model/effort remain exact. Provider addresses use a placeholder and seeded History dates are fixed; source, draft, instruction and saved text are not normalized. The first ten final observations matched the previous collection before the explicit wide-sidebar input improvement.

| Cases | Logical size / scale | Observed behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimum, narrow | 420×520, 480×640 / 1× | Saved source/rewrite, wrapping, controls, minimum extent and collapsed sidebar |
| Tiled | 360×1174 / 2× | Full 720×2348 screenshot and control bounds without virtual-screen clipping |
| Wide | 1060×780 / 1× | Visible History sidebar, two mapped headings aligned at Y=58, saved documents and controls |
| Empty, rewriting | 360×700 / 1× | Empty composer; actual streamed rewrite held before provider completion and cancelled through its button |
| Recording, processing, live-draft | 360×700 / 1× | Actual PCM capture, source-only pane, held final speech request, both Live panes and complete draft |
| Finalizing, finalizing-empty | 360×700 / 1× | Completed speech and a real held second Codex turn, with and without a previously selected conversation |

The source-only recording case enables Live and hides Draft through its actual pane button. The released compatible provider intentionally does not preview when Live is disabled. Processing holds an actual HTTP request; finalization holds provider completion after the preview and final transcript. No fixture directly sets capture-processing, live-final-entry, busy flags or record-button state. This reveals actual released behavior that the old visual fixture's substituted flags could not prove.

Every mapped control must lie within the real window and meet its minimum width. Exact observations cover 110 mapped controls across the eleven cases, plus hidden controls' sensitivity/mapping, content minimum dimensions, collapsed-sidebar width, pane alignment and separation of the Live header. Both implementations place their private window at (20,20) on a 2200×2500 virtual screen; this prevents the window manager's retained resize origin from clipping the scale-2 capture. The shared runner forwards the screen size while retaining its existing default for other callers.

After observation, real Cancel or provider completion ends the pending operation. Actual window close hides the application, and its registered `latest` action reopens the saved conversation. Original recognition is reread from SQLite rather than a stale seed object. Saved replies and clipboard contents match the release. The shared shutdown checks platform acknowledgement, child reaping, ephemeral provider-workspace removal and release of application ownership while the GLib loop can finish asynchronous teardown.

## Production repair and regression

The pre-fix native Make run passed the first nine cases and failed finalizing: Rust kept Live panes mapped while the release displayed the saved document, composer and Cancel action. Transcript, draft and provider input already matched. Released `_history_changed` reloads the selected conversation before `_workflow_finished` selects the completed entry; the native root only refreshed the list, and its completion callback ran after selection.

The root now reloads the selected entry/replies, or clears a deleted selection. A production capture callback reconciles History before selecting the completed result, preserving pruning guidance and active continuation/final-Live exclusions. Empty captures retain their early return; pending acceptance retains its existing owner. Terminal review and generated-title publication remain after selection. The additional independently collected `finalizing-empty` case proves that Live remains visible when no earlier selection exists, guarding against an unconditional hide. No test-only production API is added.

The failure is retained in `tmp/native-compact-first-make.log` and `tmp/application/run.EeQTsI/finalizing/session.17Z80n/`. Focused post-fix runs are `tmp/native-compact-finalizing-after.log` and `tmp/native-compact-finalizing-empty-after.log`. The final full compact Make command, including the reviewed wide-sidebar case, passes in `tmp/native-compact-reviewed-make.log`; evidence is under `tmp/application/run.Flkowp/` with one session per case. Both `/usr/bin/python3` and `uv` traps are positively verified before Make, then must remain unused. The old route failed that trap in `tmp/native-compact-before.log`.

## Retained contracts and verification

The former compact loop called `conversation_ui_smoke.py` for ten sizes/states. Its control bounds, minimum extents, scale, pane/header/sidebar alignment, source/reply retention and close/reopen guarantees are retained above through real application operation. The 440-line script and its shared helpers remain necessary for `linux-conversation-test` and other provider, prompt, screenshot, lifecycle, popover, scrollbar and privacy checks. This checkpoint removes the compact interpreter route; it does not claim those remaining Python consumers are gone. Lower capture, Live, History, title and transport owners retain their distinct failure/privacy/session/target contracts.

Final released logs are `tmp/native-compact-reference-final-<case>.log`, except the reviewed wide case at `tmp/native-compact-reference-wide-sidebar.log`. Ten final full-window images match the release with zero differing RGB pixels. Recording differs at four pixels in a 41×5 text-glyph region at (53,302); the same difference exists in the pre-fix and both later native captures. Exact text, geometry and controls match. `tmp/native-compact-reviewed-pixels.log` records raw ImageMagick metrics; `tmp/native-compact-recording-pixels.log` records actual differing RGB-pixel counts. Do not label all eleven images pixel-identical. Minimum/narrow/wide/2×, recording, processing and both finalizing captures were visually inspected.

The separate actual `make linux-live-stability-test linux-fluid-workspace-test` rerun passes with Python/uv trapped: eleven workflows/122 assembled states, commands/settings, 123 conversation states and fifteen actual renderer states. Application evidence is `tmp/application/run.Mysc3q/session.dzyotd/`, components `tmp/application/run.UOnTVd/session.4FetCb/`, log `tmp/native-compact-live-regression.log`. The earlier combined compact+Live invocation ended with SIGTERM/143 after compact passed, without an assertion or diagnostic; its cause is not established and that invocation is not counted as a successful full run.

Affected sibling checks pass: capture factory (six transactions/eight states), capture lifecycle (46/218), Live/capture (26/122), title jobs (28/98 plus exit), eight application shortcut workflows/34 target/store states plus pending-readiness key replacement, History recovery (15/59), and Command/Notes (19/71). Screenshot ownership passes seventeen workflows/79 states plus real SQLite-failure recovery and delayed-audio cancellation. These are existing independent contracts rerun for the changed root completion ordering, not new duplicate coverage. Logs are `tmp/native-compact-siblings.log` and `tmp/native-compact-screenshots.log`; sessions are `tmp/native-compact-sibling-evidence/session.vwz0k3/` and `tmp/native-compact-screenshots-evidence/session.JPqMtm/`.

Actual `make test` passes 139 tests, zero failures and 68 ignored environment checks across 98 suites, both strict all-target Clippy configurations, formatting and generated-document consistency. Relevant ignored GUI owners run explicitly above. Actual `make linux-python-test` passes 571 tests plus Ruff and formatting for 156 files. Full ShellCheck and diff checks pass. Logs are `tmp/native-compact-final-native.log`, `tmp/native-compact-final-python.log`, `tmp/native-compact-final-gates.log` and `tmp/native-compact-final-gates-evidence/session.SIvzOc/`. CI remains manual-only; no hosted or paid runner was used. These cached builds do not establish clean-distribution dependency/ABI acceptance.

The environment is private X11/Openbox, GTK 4.22.4, Pango 1.58.2, Libadwaita 1.9.3 and software Mesa. HOME/XDG, session/accessibility buses, network/PID/mount namespaces and clipboard are isolated; system bus and physical input/audio/GPU devices are masked. Both implementations emit transient negative-width allocation warnings while forcing compact geometry; final mapped bounds pass. Existing diagram minimum-height and PyGObject/GdkX11 warnings remain. No host input, microphone, managed credential, real-content upload or installed-app change occurs.

Production changes are +47/-10 lines; Make/shared isolation tooling +3/-11; tests/runner/support +442/-19; independent JSON observations add 3,710 lines. Documentation is separate. The three-model lineup and Qwen3-ASR 1.7B default are unchanged. Installed app/widget remain 1.6.0. Complete joined workflows, remaining Python/tooling removal, clean distribution, physical/private-Wayland acceptance and final performance measurements remain open; every whole-workflow matrix row stays Pending. No replacement, merge or Rust release is part of this checkpoint.
